paras: The New Haven posse lynching threat was a reported manhunt in New Haven, Connecticut, on August 14, 1905, in which a posse searched for an unnamed Black man accused of assaulting a nineteen-year-old white girl, intending to lynch him once he was caught. The only account found is a brief dispatch printed two days later in a South Carolina weekly, and it gives no outcome.

According to the dispatch, the man attacked a white girl, named in the printed text as "Eliza Henver," while she was on her way home on August 14. He was said to have struck her with a blackjack and then "accomplished his purpose," a phrase implying rape, and she was reported to be in serious condition. The item closed by stating that "a posse is searching for the negro with the intent to lynch him when captured."
No report of the man's capture, arrest, trial or lynching appears in the coverage, and the size and makeup of the posse were not stated.

The Watchman and Southron of Sumter, South Carolina, ran the dispatch on August 16, 1905, as a four-sentence item under a New Haven dateline. It presented the accusation as fact ("A negro assaulted"), named no source, and reported the posse's plan to lynch without comment. No Connecticut paper and no Black newspaper carrying the story was found, so the account rests on this single reprint.
